profile.freedomStatement: I want to be able to travel without worrying about money.
profile.priorities: I want to enjoy my twenties but not be careless with money.

regions.summary: Know where your money goes and put a simple budget in place.
regions.why: Everything else on your map gets easier once you can see your money clearly — this is where every journey starts.

regions.summary: Build a buffer against surprises and get on top of any debt.
regions.why: A buffer of $3,000 is the difference between a setback and a crisis. It comes before growth on purpose.

regions.summary: Turn saving into a habit and grow what you earn.
regions.why: Consistent saving is the engine for every goal on this map. This is where the habit gets built.
You told us this is what freedom looks like — it gets its own place on the map so every saving habit has somewhere to go.

regions.summary: Understand shares, funds, risk and diversification before you commit money.
regions.why: Long-term investing is the most relevant growth path for you: you have capacity and a long horizon.

regions.summary: What a deposit takes, how borrowing works, and whether property fits your plan.
regions.why: Not a priority yet because of the capital involved — it stays on the map so you can learn what it would take.

regions.summary: Side income, entrepreneurship and what it takes to build something of your own.
regions.why: Not a must, but extra income is the fastest way to raise your saving capacity.

regions.summary: How cryptocurrency works, why it swings so much, and how to think about the risk.
regions.why: Volatile and speculative; on the map for education, not as a destination.

regions.summary: Trip to Japan · Financial independence · Financial security
regions.why: This is the destination — your version of freedom, not a number someone else picked.

bridges.relationship: Knowing your spending tells you exactly how big your buffer needs to be.
bridges.why: A buffer target is just your monthly expenses multiplied — you need the first number to get the second.

bridges.relationship: With a buffer in place, your savings can stay pointed at goals instead of being raided for surprises.
bridges.why: Saving for goals before you have a buffer usually means un-saving them at the first emergency.

bridges.relationship: Every dollar you automate is a dollar closer to Trip to Japan.
bridges.why: A goal without a saving habit behind it is a wish.

bridges.requirement: Reach your Trip to Japan target
bridges.relationship: Trip to Japan is one of the pillars of your Freedom City.
bridges.why: Your definition of freedom is made of the goals you named.

bridges.relationship: Investing only works with money you won't need soon — your saving habit is what feeds it.
bridges.why: Markets reward time and consistency; the habit has to exist first.

bridges.relationship: A deposit is a very large saving goal with a deadline — the same habit, bigger numbers.
bridges.why: Deposit progress is almost entirely a function of monthly saving and time.

bridges.relationship: Extra income raises your capacity for every other goal on this map.
bridges.why: More income is the one input that makes every other target arrive sooner.

bridges.requirement: Set a saving target and learn what investing is
bridges.relationship: Digital assets amplify everything about markets — understand the ordinary version first.
bridges.why: Volatility is only survivable when it's a small part of a plan you already understand.

bridges.relationship: Long-term investing is how your Freedom City keeps being funded after the first goals are met.
bridges.why: Freedom that lasts needs money that grows without you working for every dollar of it.

steps.title: Understand where your money goes
steps.description: Track one month of spending and sort it into needs, wants and savings.
steps.why: You spend about $1,500 a month against $1,800 coming in. Knowing where it goes is the first lever you control.

steps.title: Set a simple budget
steps.description: Decide, in advance, how much goes to essentials, to enjoying life, and to your goals each month.
steps.why: A budget turns your $300 monthly surplus from an accident into a decision.

steps.title: Build a 2-month emergency buffer
steps.description: Set aside $3,000 — 2 months of your expenses — somewhere you can reach it but won't touch it.
steps.why: You have $800 saved, which covers 0.5 months of expenses. A 2-month buffer means a surprise bill doesn't derail your goals.

steps.title: Set a monthly saving target
steps.description: Pick a number you can hit every month and automate it on payday.
steps.why: You have about $300 a month left after expenses — a 17% saving rate. Automating it is the difference between hoping and doing.

steps.title: Find one way to grow your income
steps.description: More income is the fastest way to more capacity: a raise, extra hours, a new skill, or a small side project.
steps.why: Every extra dollar you earn can go straight to a goal without cutting anything you enjoy.

steps.title: Save for Trip to Japan
steps.description: Put aside about $334 a month to have $6,000 by 2028-03-01.
steps.why: At your current pace you'd reach $6,000 in 20 months, but your deadline is 18 months away. You're behind — and this map is built to fix that.

steps.title: Learn what investing actually is
steps.description: Shares, funds, returns and time — the vocabulary before the decisions.
steps.why: Understanding is free; mistakes are not. Learn the mechanics before any money moves.

steps.title: Understand risk and diversification
steps.description: Why prices move, what you can and can't control, and how spreading money reduces the damage of being wrong.
steps.why: You described your risk preference as moderate. Knowing what that means in practice keeps you from being surprised later.

steps.title: Understand what a deposit takes
steps.description: How much a deposit is, what lenders look at, and the costs beyond the price.
steps.why: Property is a very large goal; knowing the real numbers early tells you whether and when it fits your plan.

steps.title: Test one small income idea
steps.description: Pick something you could sell, make or do this month. Small and real beats big and imaginary.
steps.why: Extra income is the one lever that raises your capacity for every other goal at once.

steps.title: Understand volatility before anything else
steps.description: Why digital assets swing so hard, what that does to a plan, and how to size any exposure so it can't hurt your goals.
steps.why: This is the highest-volatility area on the map. Understanding comes first, and for many plans understanding is enough.

steps.title: Revisit what freedom means to you
steps.description: Once a quarter, re-read your freedom statement and check the map still points at it.
steps.why: You said: "I want to be able to travel without worrying about money." The whole map exists to get you there.

freedomCity.title: 🌴 Freedom City
freedomCity.narrative: Your freedom looks like trip to japan, financial independence, financial security. Every step on this map moves you closer to it.

disclaimers: Free Me provides general financial education, not personal financial advice. It doesn't know your full circumstances — consider them, and seek licensed advice for decisions that matter to you.
